title: Ceuta Border Stays Calm on Morocco's Election Day Despite Mass-Crossing Call; Four Arrested in Fnideq Clash
detail: The Ceuta-Fnideq border crossing was heavily fortified on Sep 23 as Morocco held legislative elections, after weeks of online calls — including a WhatsApp group named 'El gran asalto del 23 de septiembre' with more than 200 members — urging a repeat of the July 30-31 mass crossing. Moroccan security forces deployed reinforced contingents and water-cannon trucks along the Fnideq-Tétouan-Tangier corridor, while Spain kept extra Civil Guard units in place. In the early morning, a group of sub-Saharan migrants gathered near Fnideq and clashed with Moroccan security forces, resulting in four arrests; no mass crossing materialized and the frontier remained calm through the day. The Sep 20 and Sep 23 crossing calls both fizzled where the July surge had not, which Spanish officials attributed to the coordinated Morocco-Spain security response and the Rabat embassy's counter-disinformation campaign.

media.caption: Security forces reinforce the Ceuta-Fnideq border on Morocco's election day

title: Childhood Minister Says 54 Ceuta Minors Already Reunited With Families on Mainland, 300 More Cases Pending
detail: Speaking during a visit to Sagunto (Valencia), Minister of Childhood and Youth Sira Rego said 54 unaccompanied minors who arrived in Ceuta during the July 30-31 mass crossing have already been reunited with family members on the mainland since Aug 1, with another 300 case files currently in process. Rego said family reunification is carried out wherever the relatives are located — in Spain, elsewhere in the EU, or back in Morocco — and stressed 'it is impossible for Ceuta to handle this volume of children alone.' Her ministry, through the UMAIME unit, said it supports Ceuta's government with interviews and vulnerability assessments, and noted roughly 700 minors were relocated from Ceuta over the previous year under earlier immigration-law reforms; Ceuta has been allocated €90M for reception and transfer of minors.

media.caption: Minister Sira Rego said 54 Ceuta minors have been reunited with families on the mainland since Aug 1
